variables.name: grid/columns
variables.description: Column count, 12 — UX4G/Bootstrap. Divisible by 2, 3, 4 and 6, which is the whole reason 12 is the near-universal choice. Carbon's 16 (dropping to 8 and 4 at smaller breakpoints) is more expressive but would break UX4G parity for no gain the estate can use.

variables.name: grid/gutter
variables.description: The gap BETWEEN columns — 24px, UX4G/Bootstrap's 1.5rem exactly. Bootstrap applies half either side of each column; bind this as the layout grid's gutter and let the implementation split it.

variables.name: grid/margin/mobile
variables.description: Use for the page’s side margin on a phone — the gap between the layout grid and the viewport edge. Bind it to the frame’s horizontal padding, not to the grid’s gutter, which is `grid/gutter`.

variables.name: grid/margin/tablet
variables.description: Use for the page’s side margin on a tablet — the gap between the layout grid and the viewport edge. Bind it to the frame’s horizontal padding, not to the grid’s gutter, which is `grid/gutter`.

variables.name: grid/margin/desktop
variables.description: Use for the page’s side margin on a desktop — the gap between the layout grid and the viewport edge. Bind it to the frame’s horizontal padding, not to the grid’s gutter, which is `grid/gutter`.

variables.name: target/min
variables.description: The absolute floor — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA. Use ONLY where the spacing exception is genuinely satisfied or the target is inline in a sentence. Anything a citizen must hit on a phone deserves `comfortable`.

variables.name: target/comfortable
variables.description: WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), Level AAA, and Apple's Human Interface Guidelines minimum (44pt). The right default for a public government service: it clears the AA floor with room to spare and matches what iOS users' fingers are calibrated to.

variables.name: target/spacious
variables.description: Material Design 3 / Android's minimum touch target (48dp). Use for primary actions and anything used one-handed on the move — this is the largest of the three published floors, so meeting it satisfies all of them.

variables.name: target/spacing
variables.description: Minimum gap BETWEEN adjacent targets — Material 3's 8dp separation. It is also what makes WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception reachable: separation, not size, is what stops a 24px target being mis-tapped.

variables.name: ref/font/family/display
variables.description: The optical Display cut, for the 40-80px Display ramp. Noto Sans ships two cuts of one design: the text cut is drawn for reading at 12-24px, and at 80px its open spacing reads as loose. The Display cut tightens it. This is now genuinely LOADED (apps/hub root layout, weight 500) — for a long time it was named here and loaded nowhere, so it fell through to the text cut and the matching Figma variable could not resolve at all. LATIN ONLY: `Noto Sans Display` has no Devanagari subset and `Noto Sans Devanagari` has no Display cut, so a Hindi heading falls through to Noto Sans by design. In Figma the same cut is a STYLE of Noto Sans ("Display Medium"), not a family — see design.md. Raw type step. Prefer a text style from the Display / Headline / Title / Body / Label ramp — these are the parts those styles are assembled from.

variables.name: ref/font/family/mono
variables.description: CODE AND TECHNICAL STRINGS ONLY — token names, CSS snippets, file paths in the design-system docs. NOT for numbers, amounts or reference numbers: those want `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on Noto Sans, which aligns digits down a column while keeping them in the same typeface as the text beside them. Switching a data column to a monospace face is the clumsier fix and looks like a different design. The estate already does this correctly in the Aadhaar/PAN field, the charts, the SLA indicator and the shared DataTable. DELIBERATELY a system stack: `ui-monospace` resolves to the platform's own mono (SF Mono, Cascadia, Roboto Mono) — all well-drawn, all disambiguating 0/O and 1/l/I, and already on the device. A webfont here would download on every page to style sample code on a handful of documentation pages, which on a low-bandwidth government audience is not a trade worth making. IBM Plex Mono was set here briefly and reverted for that reason. Raw type step. Prefer a text style from the Display / Headline / Title / Body / Label ramp — these are the parts those styles are assembled from.
